title: AKS: node pools, upgrades and maintenance windows

videos.script: Lesson 10 put the shop's image in a registry. This lesson runs it on AKS, Azure's managed Kubernetes, and the first thing to learn is how little of it is managed. {{split}} Microsoft runs the control plane: the API server, etcd and the scheduler. The tier you choose decides what that is worth. Free promises nothing. Standard promises that the API server answers. {{pools}} Everything else is yours. The nodes come in pools, and every pool is a scale set of virtual machines. The system pool carries a taint that keeps your pods out, and the shop goes in a user pool. {{upgrade}} Then the versions. Each one is supported for about a year, and you move one minor version at a time, control plane first. Every node is replaced the same way. A new node is added, the old one is cordoned and drained, and your disruption budget decides how fast. {{window}} A maintenance window decides when that may start. A channel decides whether it happens at all. {{kind}} No laptop runs AKS. kind runs the same Kubernetes in Docker containers, so the drain in this lesson is real, and so is the budget refusing it. What Microsoft adds around it is taught from its documentation, and the lesson says which part is which.
